title: Do unlearning algorithms learn the right features?
abstract: arXiv:2611.06681v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine unlearning is commonly evaluated with standard post-deletion metrics that compare an unlearned model to one retrained on the remaining data. Such snapshot evaluations can conceal consequential differences in the features the two models encode. We prove that if an unlearned and a retrained model agree on their outputs but encode different features, a single gradient step on their prediction heads can break this agreement. We further show that deleting an arbitrarily small fraction of the data can cause retraining to select qualitatively different features, so matching retraining can require learning features that the full model never had. We then introduce a measure of feature recovery that separates missing from extraneous features. Across eight unlearning methods, models that perform well on standard metrics often fail to recover the retrained features. translated_title: 遗忘算法是否学到了正确的特征？
translated_abstract: 机器遗忘通常通过标准的删除后评估指标来衡量，即将遗忘后的模型与在剩余数据上重新训练的模型进行比较。这种快照式评估可能掩盖两个模型所编码特征之间的实质性差异。我们证明，如果一个遗忘模型和一个重训练模型在输出上一致但编码了不同的特征，那么只需对其预测头进行单步梯度更新就可能破坏这种一致性。我们进一步表明，删除任意小比例的数据都可能导致重训练选择性质截然不同的特征，因此要匹配重训练结果，可能需要学习完整模型从未拥有过的特征。随后，我们引入了一种特征恢复度量，将缺失特征与多余特征区分开来。在八种遗忘方法的实验中，在标准指标上表现良好的模型往往无法恢复重训练模型的特征。这种不匹配能够预测后续重新学习过程中模型与重训练模型的偏差。
tldr: 该论文证明标准的机器遗忘评估指标可能掩盖特征层面的本质差异，并提出一种区分缺失与多余特征的特征恢复度量，发现标准指标表现良好的遗忘模型往往无法恢复重训练模型的特征。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that standard machine unlearning metrics can conceal consequential feature-level differences, and introduces a feature recovery measure showing that unlearned models performing well on standard metrics often fail to recover the retrained models' features.
